what: Japan defence minister denies militarism, criticises China's 'huge arsenal'

clean_source_blocks.text: Japan's defence minister has rebutted Beijing's claim that his country is engaging in a "new militarism" - criticising China for its military expansion and lack of transparency. Speaking on the last day of a defence summit in Singapore, Shinjiro Koizumi argued it was actually China and its "huge arsenal" of weapons that was of "serious concern" to the international community. His remarks were some of the most pointed yet from Tokyo in response to China's repeated criticism of Japan's military build-up under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. The two countries have a long history of tensions stemming from Japan's invasion of China during World War Two.
Shinjiro Koizumi makes some of Tokyo's most pointed remarks yet in the dispute over Japan's military build-up.

"There's a country that has a huge arsenal of nuclear weapons and strategic bombers," he said, in a reference to China. "Japan has neither of these weapons. And yet Japan is labelled [with] 'new militarism'. Isn't it strange?" Following his speech, a representative of the Chinese military asked if Japan would issue an apology to China, South Korea and South East Asian victims in WW2. Shinjiro Koizumi sid

Last week, a day before the Singapore summit began, China's national defence ministry spokesperson Jiang Bin warned "the grey rhino of a remilitarised Japan is gathering speed" and called on the international community to "work together to contain Japan's neo-militarism". Japan has been steadily increasing its defence budget, setting spending records for 12 consecutive years. Its latest budget, approved in December by its cabinet, is for more than 9 trillion yen ($57bn, £42bn) - moving the country closer to its target of spending 2% of its GDP on the military. The Japanese government has previously insisted it does not seek war and only wants to bolster its defences.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Japan's defence minister has rebutted Beijing's claim that his country is engaging in a "new militarism" - criticising China for its military expansion and lack of transparency.

Speaking on the last day of a defence summit in Singapore, Shinjiro Koizumi argued it was actually China and its "huge arsenal" of weapons that was of "serious concern" to the international community.

His remarks were some of the most pointed yet from Tokyo in response to China's repeated criticism of Japan's military build-up under Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi.

The two countries have a long history of tensions stemming from Japan's invasion of China during World War Two.

Last week, a day before the Singapore summit began, China's national defence ministry spokesperson Jiang Bin warned "the grey rhino of a remilitarised Japan is gathering speed" and called on the international community to "work together to contain Japan's neo-militarism".

Japan has been steadily increasing its defence budget, setting spending records for 12 consecutive years. Its latest budget, approved in December by its cabinet, is for more than 9 trillion yen ($57bn, £42bn) - moving the country closer to its target of spending 2% of its GDP on the military.

The Japanese government has previously insisted it does not seek war and only wants to bolster its defences.

In his speech on Sunday at the Shangri-la Dialogue, Koizumi said it was "only natural" that every country, including Japan, updates its defences to meet new challenges and to contribute to peace in the region.

He sought to reassure the roomful of officials from Asian countries, including several that were invaded by Japan in WW2, by promising Japan would proceed "with a high degree of transparency" and engage in constant dialogue with other countries.

"What are we developing these capabilities for? And based on what thinking? Japan will move forward while making a clear explanation to the international community," he said.

Koizumi refuted the idea that Japan was engaged in "new militarism" saying it was "nothing further from the truth".

"There's a country that has a huge arsenal of nuclear weapons and strategic bombers," he said, in a reference to China. "Japan has neither of these weapons.  And yet Japan is labelled [with] 'new militarism'. Isn't it strange?"

Following his speech, a representative of the Chinese military asked if Japan would issue an apology to China, South Korea and South East Asian victims in WW2.

Shinjiro Koizumi sid

payload.title: Japanin puolustusministeri torjui Kiinan väitteet uudesta militarismista
payload.summary: Japanin puolustusministeri Shinjiro Koizumi kiisti Singaporessa Kiinan väitteet Japanin uudesta militarismista ja arvosteli Kiinan asevarustelua sekä läpinäkyvyyden puutetta.
payload.content:
Japanin puolustusministeri Shinjiro Koizumi on torjunut Pekingin väitteet siitä, että Japani olisi ajautumassa uuteen militarismiin. Singaporessa järjestetyn puolustushuippukokouksen päätöspäivänä puhunut Koizumi käänsi arvostelun Kiinaan ja sanoi maan suuren asearsenaalin sekä sotilaallisen läpinäkyvyyden puutteen olevan vakava huolenaihe kansainväliselle yhteisölle.

## Tokio vastaa Pekingin arvosteluun

Koizumin puhe oli yksi Japanin tähänastisista suorimmista vastauksista Kiinan toistuviin syytöksiin. Peking on arvostellut Japanin puolustusmenojen kasvua pääministeri Sanae Takaichin kaudella ja kuvannut kehitystä vaaralliseksi uudelleenaseistautumiseksi.

Koizumi viittasi puheessaan Kiinaan sanomalla, että alueella on maa, jolla on suuri määrä ydinaseita ja strategisia pommikoneita. Hänen mukaansa Japanilla ei ole kumpiakaan näistä aseista. Koizumi piti ristiriitaisena sitä, että Japania kuvataan tällaisessa tilanteessa uuden militarismin kautta.

Puheen jälkeen Kiinan armeijan edustaja kysyi, aikooko Japani esittää anteeksipyynnön Kiinalle, Etelä-Korealle ja Kaakkois-Aasian toisen maailmansodan uhreille. Maiden välisiä jännitteitä varjostaa yhä Japanin hyökkäys Kiinaan toisen maailmansodan aikana.

## Puolustusmenot ovat kasvaneet pitkään

Kiinan puolustusministeriön tiedottaja Jiang Bin varoitti viime viikolla, päivää ennen Singaporen kokouksen alkua, että Japanin uudelleenmilitarisoituminen on kiihtymässä. Hän kehotti kansainvälistä yhteisöä toimimaan Japanin niin sanotun uusmilitarismin hillitsemiseksi.

Japani on kasvattanut puolustusbudjettiaan tasaisesti, ja puolustusmenot ovat nousseet ennätystasolle 12 peräkkäisenä vuonna. Viimeisin hallituksen joulukuussa hyväksymä budjetti on yli 9 biljoonaa jeniä eli noin 57 miljardia dollaria ja 42 miljardia puntaa. Se vie Japania lähemmäs tavoitetta käyttää puolustukseen kaksi prosenttia bruttokansantuotteestaan.

Japanin hallitus on aiemmin korostanut, ettei se tavoittele sotaa vaan pyrkii vahvistamaan omaa puolustustaan. Koizumin puhe osoittaa, että Tokio haluaa vastata Kiinan arvosteluun aiempaa terävämmin samalla, kun alueen turvallisuuskeskustelu kiristyy.

Koizumi arvosteli Kiinan asevarustelua ja sotilaallisen läpinäkyvyyden puutetta.
